question: At pin, does scoring-cap / score-snapshot logic create a blind-spot where small or never-scored subnets are starved on a fresh snapshot or surface via stale snapshot/mtime rather than merit? Cite SHA:path:line and bytes_read for each affirmative subclaim.

hypothesis.summary: Blind-spot / inversion: cap or snapshot freshness/mtime can dominate merit for never-scored or small subnets.
hypothesis.note: Candidates are search starts only — not proof. No line numbers asserted until Tracer fetch.

expected_evidence_form: schema v1 bundle(s) with fetch_method, bytes_read, citations[{sha,path,line}], falsifier per subclaim; or NOT_OBSERVABLE naming what was searched

falsifier.probe: Fetch candidates at pin via raw->api->mc_paste; locate cap/universe/mtime/freshness gates and call sites
falsifier.expected: Cite concrete mechanism bytes supporting blind-spot claim, or NOT_OBSERVABLE with search scope
falsifier.refutes_if: No supporting mechanism after fetch ladder, OR cited bytes do not support starvation/stale-vs-merit claim

pass_rule: Affirmative subclaims require SHA:path:line + bytes_read + fetch_method. No narrative-only answers.
notes: Opened after Gate 0b CLEARED. Dispatch Tracer only after MC says go.
